blocks.content: Quiz: Which of these belongs in the "must-have" column when defining SpeedBlip's MVP?
Tap an option below to answer:
ISP comparison charts showing your speed vs neighbors in your area
This is a nice-to-have feature that adds context but is not needed for the product to solve the core problem of monitoring your own connection.
This is a nice-to-have feature that adds context but is not needed for the product to solve the core problem of monitoring your own connection.
Automatic background speed tests with download, upload, and ping
Correct. Without automatic measurement, SpeedBlip does not function. This is the core behavior the one-sentence definition describes - it is non-negotiable for the MVP.
Correct. Without automatic measurement, SpeedBlip does not function. This is the core behavior the one-sentence definition describes - it is non-negotiable for the MVP.
PDF export of historical speed data
Useful for some users, but not required for the product to work. Users can already see their history in the app - export is a nice-to-have enhancement.
Useful for some users, but not required for the product to work. Users can already see their history in the app - export is a nice-to-have enhancement.
Multi-device tracking across a home network
Multi-device support adds significant complexity and is not required for SpeedBlip to solve the problem for a single user. It belongs in the nice-to-have column.
Multi-device support adds significant complexity and is not required for SpeedBlip to solve the problem for a single user. It belongs in the nice-to-have column.
